subject: history_social
passage: When the modern Olympic Games were founded in the 1890s, their organizers looked to ancient Greece for an ideal. Ancient athletes, they claimed, were amateurs who competed purely for honor, receiving nothing but a crown of olive leaves for victory. Professional sport, in this view, was a modern corruption of the Greek spirit.
passage_b: It is true that the official prize at Olympia was an olive crown. But historian Nikos Andreou points out that victors could expect far more once they returned home. Their cities rewarded them with cash, statues, and free meals for life, and at other Greek festivals winners received valuable prizes such as large jars of olive oil. The amateur athlete, Andreou concludes, was largely an invention of the modern Olympic movement.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the organizers' claim in Text 1?

choices.A: By pointing out that ancient winners in fact received valuable rewards
choices.B: By arguing that the modern Olympics should stop awarding prizes
choices.C: By agreeing that ancient athletes competed only for the honor of winning
choices.D: By claiming that olive crowns were never given to winners at Olympia

explanation.why: Text 1 reports the organizers' claim that ancient athletes received "nothing but a crown of olive leaves." Text 2 grants that the olive crown was the official prize but says winners received "cash, statues, and free meals for life" at home and valuable prizes elsewhere. So Text 2 would reject the image of the purely amateur Greek athlete.
explanation.A: Correct. Text 2 shows that victors received money and other valuable rewards from their cities and at other festivals.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 discusses ancient rewards and never recommends any change to the modern Games.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 lists cash, statues, meals, and olive oil as rewards, so athletes did not compete for honor alone.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says, "It is true that the official prize at Olympia was an olive crown."
